summary: Executed backend + frontend reconciliation regression on public URL. Verified calculation formula, required API response fields, save/list/select/print flows, and permission behavior. Found one critical UI/backend permission mismatch for enter_deposits-only users.

integration_issues.issue: User with enter_deposits=true and view_reports=false is blocked from /bank/:bankId/reconciliation by ProtectedRoute(permission='view_reports'), so cannot reach UI to save reconciliation despite backend allowing POST with enter_deposits.

action_items: Align reconciliation page access permission with save permission requirement (enter_deposits).
Decide intended policy: either allow enter_deposits users to open reconciliation page, or change backend save permission to match view_reports and update requirement/UI messaging.
critical_code_review_comments: Permission contract is inconsistent across layers: frontend route gate uses view_reports while reconciliation POST requires enter_deposits.
backend/server.py is monolithic (>1100 lines), increasing regression risk for finance-critical changes.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Validated on https://scanner-ocr-test.preview.emergentagent.com. Reconciliation math/status/print/history are working. Reproduce critical mismatch by logging in as enter_deposits-only user and opening /bank/banque-misr/reconciliation; app redirects to '/'.
rca of the issue: RCA: route protection mismatch. In frontend App.js, reconciliation route is wrapped with ProtectedRoute(permission='view_reports'). Backend POST /api/banks/{bank_id}/reconciliations is guarded by require_permission('enter_deposits'). This split causes enter_deposits-only users to be denied UI access even though backend authorizes save. Reproduction: create user {enter_deposits:true, view_reports:false}, login, navigate to /bank/banque-misr/reconciliation, observe redirect to '/'.
